victim_age: Not stated for a single victim; two child victims: Akash aged 5 years, Nikita aged 2 years
accused_victim_relationship: Relative: co-wife (the deceased Mandabai was the first wife of the accused's husband); the accused was step-mother of the two children
evidence_type: Circumstantial (primary); chemical analysis of frock; recovery of kerosene can (disbelieved); dying declarations; extra-judicial confession (disbelieved); medical evidence
confession: Extra-judicial confession to father-in-law (PW-1) that kerosene was sprinkled and fire set; disbelieved by the High Court as not trustworthy and not relied on by the Supreme Court
aggravating_circumstances: Death of three persons, two of them small children; incident described as gruesome
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302 and 436; sentence imposed (amount/term not stated in judgment)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed (judgment dated 12.10.2017)
neutral_facts: On the intervening night of 2 and 3 August 2006, at about 2.30 to 3.00 am, a fire broke out in a small house of three rooms. The house was occupied by the accused, the accused's husband, the husband's first wife, the first wife's two children, the husband's parents and a servant who occupied one room. The husband had gone to another town that day to buy tractor tyres, and the mother-in-law had gone to her daughter's home. The accused came out of the house without any injury. The first wife and her daughter ran out with burn injuries, while the son died inside the house. The father-in-law, who had been sleeping on a cot outside, woke in the confusion and arranged for a jeep to take the injured to hospital. The first wife and daughter died the next day from their burns. Police seized the daughter's burnt frock from the scene under a panchnama and sent it for chemical analysis, which reported kerosene residues. A kerosene can said to smell of kerosene was recovered from nearby bushes at the accused's instance, but it was not sent for chemical analysis. The father-in-law stated that the accused had made an extra-judicial confession to him that kerosene had been sprinkled and the fire set. A sister of the first wife gave evidence of an oral dying declaration, and a police head constable recorded a separate dying declaration. The first wife's declaration said the household slept in the house with a lantern lit at night, and that cooking and tractor diesel were kept there. Medical evidence was presented on the cause of the deaths.
physical_harm: Deaths of the first wife (Mandabai) and daughter (Nikita) from burn injuries the next day in hospital; son (Akash) burnt to death inside the house; accused unhurt
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.302 and s.436); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Destruction of the house and adjoining cowshed
motive: Not identified. Alleged by the High Court: desire for domestic dominance and removal of the first wife and children; the Supreme Court found this could not be accepted as a strong motive
key_evidence_accepted: Chemical analysis of Nikita's frock reporting kerosene residues, taken at face value but held insufficient alone; deceased's declaration that kerosene was used for lanterns and cooking; admitted layout of the house and non-injury of other occupants; PW-1's account that he was sleeping outside
witness_credibility: High Court disbelieved PW-1's extra-judicial confession account and the oral dying declaration; the Supreme Court relied on PW-1's account of sleeping outside and waking on the accused's shouts, and held the disbelieved evidence could not support conviction
post_offence_conduct: Came out of the house unhurt and raised shouts; High Court inferred she did not alarm or rescue the others, which the Supreme Court held could not by itself establish guilt
bail_history: On interim bail at the time of the Supreme Court judgment
trial_duration: offence: 2/3 August 2006; trial judgment: 16.11.2007; High Court: 12.10.2017; Supreme Court: August 10, 2021
legal_representation: Appellant: Sudhanshu S. Choudhari, Adv. State of Maharashtra (respondent): Sachin Patil, Rahul Chitnis, Aaditya A. Pande, Geo Joseph, Advs.
investigation_status: Complaint lodged by father-in-law implicating the accused; investigation by PSI Phad; trial completed; charge sheet not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 436 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside, accused acquitted
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain pointing to guilt that must be true, not may be true; suspicion cannot replace proof; failure to explain under s.106 is only an additional link once other links are proved
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Devilal v. State of Rajasthan (2019) 19 SCC 447
other_sentence_order: Appellant set at liberty; bail bond discharged
